title: Witty Alien👽 VS Magnus Carlsen🐐
reviewNotes: All 42 saved states and narration reviewed. This is a middlegame attack from Witty Alien versus Magnus: Re1?/Rb1+/Kd2/Qd5+ and the Bc4 resource. Illustrated lines retain many pawns, queens and rooks; the clip returns to the resignation after Qd5+. Narration mentions a simple endgame after hypothetical trades, but does not present a sparse endgame study or a worked conversion. Retained as a searchable channel tactic, not promoted to an Endgame Stories endgame lesson.
transcript: Rook E1 is a losing blunder that gives up the game instantly. But why should you care? Well, look at who is playing with the white pieces. It is Magnus Carlsen, the strongest chess player ever. But okay, so what? Magnus does lose games every now and then in online blitz. But that is not the point. Look at his opponent. It is my boy Witty Alien, the inventor of the Alien Gambit. You see, Witty was actually losing for pretty much the majority of the game. But then, he found an opportunity here after opening up his rook and his bishop and his queen towards white's king. And after Magnus played rook to E1, the evaluation went from completely winning for white to completely lost. And that is because of rook to B1 check, forcing the king to come out, and then queen to D5. The queen and the rook beautifully coordinate to kick the king out. Of course, if the king comes out here, now you can take the rook with check. And you better believe that even against Magnus Carlsen, a player like Witty is going to win in such a simple textbook end game. But what Magnus might have missed is the fact that after this check, if he tries to go to E2, now there is bishop to C4. The bishop comes back taking even more squares from the king. And the king doesn't really have any place that it can go to apart from E3, which would still allow this. So, Magnus would actually have to give up the queen. And you better believe that once again, Witty is going to be able to win this end game. So, actually after Queen to D5 check, Magnus Carlsen resigned the game. And the coolest part is that Witty had almost no reaction to this achievement. >> I don't know what he's doing. Very excited. >> Congrats, brother Witty. You are a legend.
